title: Constructible comparison
statement:
For Noetherian $\Lambda$, a sheaf on $X_{\Proet}$ is constructible if locally on $X$
a finite partition into constructible locally closed strata makes it locally
constant of finite type on each stratum.

Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For a discrete Noetherian
$\Lambda$, every constructible pro-étale $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf is classical.
The functor $\nu_X^*$ gives an equivalence from constructible étale sheaves of
$\Lambda$-modules to $\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$, and an equivalence
$D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ of bounded constructible derived
categories.

proof.text: For discrete $\Lambda$, the finite constant local models in [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are constant sheaves of finitely presented $\Lambda$-modules, using the coefficient identification $\Lambda_X=\nu_X^*\Lambda_{X,\Et}$ in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Over the Noetherian ring $\Lambda$, finite-type models are finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]; a finite presentation conversely supplies finitely many generators. Thus the local finite-partition condition in the first paragraph is exactly the affine-local constructibility condition, with no Noetherian hypothesis on $X$. On qcqs $X$ this also yields the finite global stratification required by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Quasi-compactness and the affine basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] give a finite affine open cover $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ of $X$ with finite partitions $V_j=\coprod_k Z_{jk}$ into constructible locally closed subschemes of $V_j$ carrying these models. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratification-local-gluing-core] there is a finite stratification of $X$ by locally closed subschemes $T_c$ whose underlying sets are constructible in $X$, pairwise disjoint and covering, such that every stratum immersion $T_c\to X$ factors by a scheme morphism $h_c:T_c\to Z_{jk}$ through one local stratum immersion $Z_{jk}\to V_j\to X$. Pulling back the local constant trivializations of $F|_{Z_{jk}}$ along $h_c$, with the composition compatibility of restrictions in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], gives $F|_{T_c}$ a finite constant local model with the same finitely presented modules, as required. Conversely, intersecting a finite global stratification with an affine open retains locally closed pieces that are constructible in the sense of [def-weil-constructible-subset]: an open retrocompact $A\subset X$ restricts to a retrocompact open there because every quasi-compact open of that affine open is also a quasi-compact open of $X$. The displayed constant models restrict as well.

proof.text: Use classicality in the precise sense of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map]: for every pro-etale affine presentation $U\cong\varprojlim_{i\in I}U_i$ indexed by a small cofiltered category in the fixed site universes, the continuity map $\varinjlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U_i)\to F(U)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules. The scalar action on sections comes from $\Lambda\to\Lambda_X(V)$. On a general $X$ use these inverse-limit presentations; the identification with affine ind-etale objects is only used over an affine base. For qcqs $X$, apply [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical], including its final locally stratified clause, to conclude that every constructible $F$ is classical; by step 1 this covers both the local definition of the first paragraph and $\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)$. The empty scheme and zero sheaf are included.

proof.text:
Use the affine-local definition of constructible etale modules in [def-pe-etale-constructible-module]; the coefficient ring is Noetherian, and the constant models need only be finitely generated as modules. Let $G$ be an etale constructible $\Lambda$-module sheaf. On each constructible locally closed stratum $i:Z	o X$ of a local stratification, the first, underived inverse-image clause of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], used in the inverse direction, identifies $i^*
u_X^*G$ with $
u_Z^*i^*G$. The models of $i^*G$ are finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], so [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] shows that this restriction is a pro-etale local system with the same finite-presentation models. These affine-local strata, globalized on qcqs $X$ as in step 1, show that $
u_X^*G$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The functor is fully faithful on all module sheaves by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Conversely let $F$ be constructible. By [det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical] and [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], put $G=
u_{X,*}F$ and obtain $
u_X^*G\cong F$. For each stratum $i:Z	o X$ on which $i^*F$ is locally constant of finite type, its models are finitely presented by the same algebra lemma, and [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] supplies an etale local system $H$ of finitely presented modules with $
u_Z^*H\cong i^*F$. Pullback compatibility gives $
u_Z^*i^*G\cong
u_Z^*H$. Full faithfulness on $Z$ lifts this isomorphism and its inverse uniquely; their composites lift the identity, so $i^*G\cong H$. Applying this to the restriction of a global stratification of $F$ to each affine open (step 1), the very same strata therefore make $G$ etale constructible. This proves essential surjectivity and the constructible sheaf equivalence, without any separate gluing assertion.

source.place: part (1), pullback to strata, construction G=nu_*F, and reflection of the stratum isomorphisms

proof.text:
Classicality for complexes means classicality of every cohomology sheaf, with the same presentation and module conventions, by clause 4 of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map]. Here $D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ has the bounded constructible-cohomology meaning of [def-pe-etale-constructible-module]. By [sk-prop-sf-comparison], the bounded-below derived unit is an isomorphism for our discrete Noetherian $\Lambda$; this verifies the hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]. We may therefore use its inverse equivalences on $D^+$ and the subcategory with classical cohomology. Exactness of $
u_X^*$ from [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] gives $H^q(
u_X^*L)\cong
u_X^*H^q(L)$: applying an exact functor preserves the kernels and images defining cohomology. For $L\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, step 3 makes these sheaves constructible and they vanish outside the finite cohomological interval of $L$, so its pullback belongs to $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ as defined in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Conversely, for $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$, its cohomology sheaves are classical by step 2 ([det-pe-constructible-comparison-classical]). The derived equivalence supplies $L=R
u_{X,*}K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ with $
u_X^*L\cong K$. Thus $
u_X^*H^q(L)\cong H^q(K)$. Step 3 and full faithfulness identify $H^q(L)$ with the constructible etale antecedent $
u_{X,*}H^q(K)$. If $H^q(K)=0$, faithfulness forces $1_{H^q(L)}=0$, so $H^q(L)=0$. Consequently $L$ is bounded in the same finite interval and lies in $D^b_c$. Restricting the fully faithful derived equivalence to these full subcategories proves the claimed bounded constructible equivalence.
